exposure: Prophylactic anti-D immunoglobulin (single 300-ug dose at 28 weeks' gestation)
outcome: Serological detectability of prophylactic anti-D immunoglobulin at term
cohort: 915 RhD-negative women with singleton pregnancies who received routine antenatal Rhesus immune globulin at 28 weeks and delivered at Kayseri City Hospital between January 2023 and January 2025.
finding: A single 300-ug anti-D dose at 28 weeks leaves nearly two-thirds of RhD-negative women serologically undetectable for anti-D at term if the prophylaxis-to-delivery interval exceeds 10 weeks.
followup_time: From 28 weeks' gestation until delivery (mean 69 days after prophylaxis)
gest_age: Prophylaxis administered at 28 ± 2 weeks; delivery occurred at 38 ± 2 weeks.
